# Egregor

> Egregor is a local-first desktop application that orchestrates Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok and 300+ other models (via OpenRouter) into a structured multi-AI "Consilium" — where models debate, cross-check each other, and synthesize answers no single model could produce alone. Its flagship use case: smart-contract security audits for $0.30–2.00 instead of the $5,000–50,000 charged by traditional auditors.

Egregor runs entirely on the user's own computer. AI models receive only small fragments of context — no single model ever sees the full project — so the user's data, code, and ideas stay private and never become training data for AI corporations.

Key differentiators:
- Multi-AI Consilium with defined expert roles (Security, Reasoning, Devil's Advocate, Moderator)
- Anti-Groupthink Engine — prevents models from collapsing into polite agreement
- Code Review Pipeline — 5-step smart-contract audit (3 of 5 models are free)
- Confidence Map — every verdict comes with a 1–5 trust score
- Context Compression Engine — 100k tokens compressed to ~5k (20× cheaper)
- Semantic Cache — repeated questions answered from cache at zero cost
- Runs on free models for ~80% of tasks; full privacy, local-first, 6 languages
